subject: Live echo / delayed token emit — customer snapshot + temporary canary plan
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@orchidapp.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Orchid App Support <support@orchidapp.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live session — repeated tokens / sluggish streaming

Hi Alex,

We started seeing an issue in our live chat sessions around 08:45 PDT where streaming responses are either delayed by several seconds or emit repeated token fragments (echoing the last 4–6 tokens). This is impacting our agent UI and causing spurious duplicate messages. Happened on both us-west and us-east regions.

Attached are a short session log and a screenshot from our UI. Happy to provide more traces if you point me to what you need.

Can you confirm receipt and tell us what temporary steps we should take while you investigate? This is customer-facing and we’re getting pushback from our support team.

Thanks,
Elena
Customer Success Manager
Orchid App

Attachment: orchid_session_logs_20260825.txt (text)
Attachment: screenshot_stream_health.png (image)
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@orchidapp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Orchid App Support <support@orchidapp.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live session — repeated tokens / sluggish streaming

Hi Elena — thanks for the prompt report and attachments. We got them and have triaged the initial signals.

Short summary: we’re seeing elevated token emit latency on a small subset of streaming endpoints in us-west which can manifest as delayed chunks or small repeated token sequences when the KV cache repopulates during autoscaling events. We’ve opened STREAM-1247 (linked below) and are running targeted telemetry to isolate affected shards.

Immediate customer-facing mitigations you can try while we work on a fix:
- Switch to the non-streaming / synchronous response endpoint for the most critical flows (slightly higher end-to-end latency but avoids chunking artifacts).
- Add a client-side dedupe on messages arriving within 500ms of each other with overlapping suffixes.
- If you can, pin requests to region us-east temporarily (we see lower incidence there right now).
- Reduce max_tokens to 256 for streaming sessions that need low risk of echo while we stabilize.

We’ll put a temporary canary in place routing a small percentage of your traffic to a legacy model-variant that is not hit by the current emit-path regression. Marissa and Hannah are on the operations plan for that canary. We aim to have the canary configured in the next 90 minutes and will update you with results and a rollback window.

Can you confirm which org-id and a sample request-id from one of the affected sessions (request ids from the session logs are ideal)? I’ve pointed the ops team at the attachments already.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena@orchidapp.com>, Orchid App Support <support@orchidapp.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live session — repeated tokens / sluggish streaming

Looping in operational steps and timeline. 

Planned actions (ops):
1) 10:10 PDT — deploy canary routing 5% of Orchid traffic to model-legacy-v2 in us-west only (no config change required on customer side). This variant uses a different emit path and avoids the async KV repopulation that’s currently noisy.
2) 10:15–10:45 PDT — monitor token latency, chunk size distribution, and error rates. If the canary shows stable emits and no repeats, we’ll ramp to 25% and then to 100% for affected customers as needed.
3) If the canary fails, immediate rollback to standard routing; we’ll enable short lived request-level prefix caching (30s TTL) at the edge to reduce rehydration events.

Temporary client config recommendations to share with the Orchid front-end team (customer-facing):
- Backoff and dedupe: on receipt of a repeated suffix, wait 300–600ms before replaying user-visible content.
- Streaming timeout: set token-stream-window to 1500ms for UI that aggregates chunks before render.
- Fallback mode: add a quick retry path that calls the non-streaming API after 1 failed streaming attempt.

Operational notes for Redwood internal team: Hannah — please prepare a short telemetry dashboard that shows per-shard emit latency and the percentage of sessions with >=1 repeated chunk. Sean — prepare a postmortem template and a proposed customer advisory draft if we need to extend the canary longer than 6 hours.

I’ll update Orchid at each step and post the canary results to the Drive link.

— Marissa
Sr. Product Manager, Platform Reliability
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Related: https://drive.redwood.com/s/Orchid-20260825-session-logs; JIRA: STREAM-1247
Attachment referenced: orchid_session_logs_20260825.txt
From: Elena Rossi <elena@orchidapp.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Orchid App Support <support@orchidapp.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live session — repeated tokens / sluggish streaming

Thanks — appreciate the quick coordination. We confirmed the canary routing to model-legacy-v2 for a small cohort and see a marked reduction in echoed fragments in the first 30 minutes of traffic. Our support team is switching the most exposed customers to the canary cohort.

Two asks from Orchid:
1) Can you confirm whether this qualifies for an SLA investigation/credit? We’ll pull together impact windows if necessary.
2) Once you have the postmortem, can you include the timeline and the permanent fix plan so our engineering team can plan any client changes?

We’ll keep the canary running until you advise. Looping in our engineering lead if you need additional logs or instrumentation.

— Elena
Elena Rossi
Customer Success Manager, Orchid App
